speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have been experiencing headaches and worsening vision over the last three weeks. To help me understand your condition, have these visual changes been central, peripheral, or affecting both eyes equally?

speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old woman. The patient reports a 3-week history of headache and progressively worsening vision. She has not noticed any other symptoms, including no recent weight changes, no fevers, no night sweats, and no pain elsewhere in the body.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your age and the progressive nature of your vision loss alongside headaches, are your vision changes unilateral or bilateral, and have you noticed any specific visual phenomena like "cortical blindness" or a loss of color?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Headache. I also have Worsening vision over the past 3 weeks, No weight changes, No fevers, No night sweats, No other pain.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Giant Cell Arteritis (Temporal Arteritis).
Based on your age, new onset headache, and progressive vision changes without systemic symptoms, this is highly suggestive of vasculitis affecting the ophthalmic arteries. Immediate treatment with high-dose steroids is required to prevent permanent blindness, but I must confirm this with an urgent ESR and CRP blood test before finalizing the plan. REQUEST TEST: ESR, CRP.
